subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Who wrote 'An Inspector Calls'?
options: J.B. Priestley
George Bernard Shaw
Arthur Miller
Oscar Wilde
questions.explain: The play was written by the socialist playwright J.B. Priestley.

questions.q: In what year is the action of the play set?
questions.explain: The play is set on an evening in spring 1912, two years before the First World War.

questions.q: In what year was the play written and first performed?
questions.explain: Priestley wrote and first staged the play in 1945, at the end of the Second World War.

questions.q: What is the name of the police inspector who visits the Birlings?
options: Inspector Goole
Inspector Ghoul
Inspector Gould
Inspector Grimes
questions.explain: His name 'Goole' is a homophone of 'ghoul', hinting at his mysterious, otherworldly nature.

questions.q: By which two names is the dead young woman known in the play?
options: Eva Smith and Daisy Renton
Eva Smith and Edna Croft
Sheila Birling and Daisy Renton
Daisy Renton and Edna Smith
questions.explain: She is referred to as Eva Smith and later used the name Daisy Renton.

questions.q: Into how many acts is the play divided?
options: Three
One
Five
Two
questions.explain: The play is structured in three acts with continuous, real-time action.

questions.q: To whom is Sheila Birling engaged at the start of the play?
options: Gerald Croft
Eric Birling
Inspector Goole
Arthur Birling
questions.explain: The play opens with a dinner celebrating Sheila's engagement to Gerald Croft.

questions.q: What is Arthur Birling's occupation?
options: A prosperous factory owner and manufacturer
A retired police officer
A local schoolteacher
A shop assistant at Milwards
questions.explain: Arthur Birling is a wealthy industrialist who owns Birling and Company.

questions.q: In which fictional industrial town is the play set?
options: Brumley
Brumford
Bromley
Bramhall
questions.explain: The Birlings live in the fictional North Midlands industrial town of Brumley.

questions.q: Why did Arthur Birling dismiss Eva Smith from his factory?
options: She led workers asking for higher wages
She stole money from the firm
She was rude to a customer
She refused to work overtime
questions.explain: Birling sacked Eva for helping to organise a strike for a small pay rise.

questions.q: Why was Eva Smith dismissed from Milwards, the department store?
options: Sheila had her sacked out of jealousy
Mrs Birling reported her to the manager
Gerald complained about her service
Eric caused a disturbance in the shop
questions.explain: Sheila had Eva dismissed in a fit of jealousy after imagining Eva was mocking her.

questions.q: What was the nature of Gerald Croft's involvement with Daisy Renton?
options: He kept her as his mistress before ending the affair
He employed her as a shop assistant
He reported her to the charity committee
He offered her marriage
questions.explain: Gerald installed Daisy Renton in rooms and had an affair with her the previous summer.

questions.q: Why is Mrs Birling implicated in Eva Smith's death?
options: As charity chair she refused Eva the help she requested
She had Eva arrested by the police
She dismissed Eva from the factory
She encouraged Sheila to complain about Eva
questions.explain: Mrs Birling, chairing the Brumley Women's Charity, turned away the pregnant Eva who sought aid.

questions.q: What is the central message the Inspector delivers about society?
options: That people are collectively responsible for one another
That class distinctions must be strengthened
That charity should be left to the wealthy
That the young should defer to their elders
questions.explain: The Inspector argues 'we are members of one body' and responsible for each other.

questions.q: Why is Birling's confident claim that the Titanic is 'unsinkable' an example of dramatic irony?
options: The audience knows the Titanic sank in 1912
The Titanic had not yet been built in 1912
Birling secretly knows it will sink
The Titanic is a fictional ship in the play
questions.explain: The 1945 audience knew the Titanic sank on its maiden voyage, undermining Birling's judgement.

questions.q: How does the play primarily contrast the older and younger Birlings?
options: The younger characters accept responsibility while the elders resist it
The elders reform while the younger stay unchanged
Both generations refuse to change at all
Only Gerald and Eric show any guilt
questions.explain: Sheila and Eric feel genuine guilt, whereas Mr and Mrs Birling dismiss their part.

questions.q: Why did Priestley set a 1945 play in the year 1912?
options: To use hindsight to expose the complacency of the old order
Because the play is a historical documentary of 1912
To avoid censorship of contemporary events
Because 1912 was when Priestley was born
questions.explain: The 1912 setting lets Priestley use dramatic irony to criticise pre-war capitalist complacency.

questions.q: What is the effect of the play's continuous, real-time structure?
options: It builds relentless tension as the family is interrogated
It allows several years to pass between acts
It creates comic relief between scenes
It shifts the setting to many locations
questions.explain: The unbroken real-time action keeps the pressure on the characters mounting throughout.

questions.q: The Inspector says the lesson will be taught 'in fire and blood and anguish' if it is ignored. Which theme does this most directly express?
options: Social responsibility
Gender inequality
The generation gap
Romantic love
questions.explain: The warning stresses the consequences of failing in collective, social responsibility.

questions.q: A student argues one character changes most through the play, moving from careless privilege to genuine moral awareness. Which character best fits?
options: Sheila Birling
Arthur Birling
Sybil Birling
Gerald Croft
questions.explain: Sheila is transformed by the Inspector, fully accepting guilt while her parents do not.

questions.q: At the very end, a phone call announces a real inspector is coming to ask questions about a girl's death. What is the dramatic effect of this ending?
options: It creates a cyclical structure that reopens the family's guilt
It resolves all the tension neatly and happily
It proves Inspector Goole was a genuine policeman
It removes any sense of consequence for the Birlings
questions.explain: The final twist loops the action back, forcing the family to face judgement again.

questions.q: Birling dismisses the risk of war, saying the world is developing so fast that conflict is impossible. Applying your contextual knowledge, why would a 1945 audience find this striking?
options: They had lived through two world wars since 1912
They believed Birling's prediction was correct
They had never heard of the First World War
They thought 1912 was a peaceful decade
questions.explain: Having endured both world wars, the audience sees Birling's confidence as deeply misguided.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Literature (1ET0) specification; An Inspector Calls
